Assessment adjusted using the Financial Stability Report: The FOMC held the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50 percent and continued balance-sheet runoff ($60B Treasuries, $35B MBS), with a floor-system implementation (IORB 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%, repo 5.5%). Macro tone remains cautiously positive—solid growth, strong job gains, and easing but still elevated inflation—with a high bar for rate cuts pending “greater confidence” on disinflation.

FSR insights temper this optimism. The report highlights notable vulnerabilities and risks: stress in commercial real estate (especially offices) with rising vacancy weighing on credit quality; valuation pressures in some asset classes; persistent structural vulnerabilities in money market funds and broader short-term funding markets; elevated interest rate volatility and leveraged positions in Treasury futures among hedge funds; and macro tail risks from high public debt, geopolitical tensions, and potential spillovers from foreign (e.g., China) weakness. These stability concerns argue for continued vigilance even as the cyclical data are firm.

Net tone: cautiously optimistic on activity, vigilant on inflation, and more guarded due to identified financial stability vulnerabilities and market-structure risks.
